DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.corn.ph DILG OPINION No. 128 s. 2022 October 12, 2022 DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENIERO Regional Director, DILG Region VI P. Aquino St., Fort San Pedro, Iloilo Dear RD Ingeniero: This pertains to your Memorandum dated 10 May 2022 requesting for guidance on the settlement of boundary dispute between Barangay Agcalaga and Barangay Alibunan over Sitio Bolicao and the alleged non-consultation of the municipal government, particularly the Office of Sangguniang Bayan of Calinog with the barangay officials of Barangay Agcalaga. As you have presented in your Memorandum: I. A complaint was forwarded to the municipal government of Calinog and in reply thereto Mayor Francisco L. Calvo submitted the following information: ii iv v. vi. vii Proper consultations were done as evidenced by attendance sheets of consultative meetings signed 15 July 2019, 03 March 2020, 14 July 2021 and 08 November 2021; Resolution No. 2022-002 was adopted by the Sangguniang Bayan on IO January 2022 taking cognizance of the disputed Sitio Bolicao as part of Brgy. Alibunan and not of Brgy. Agcalaga as contained in the Barangay Boundary and Parcellary Map surveyed on January 15, February 18-22 and March 3-7 by the Surveys and Control Section of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources; It was alleged that in 2014, the same year when then President Benigno Aquino mandated for political boundaries to be identified, Brgy. Agcalaga listed Sitio Bolicao as part of their territory following the commencement of the Jalaur River Dam Project; Survey PB 06-00037 belied Brgy. Agcalaga's claim and affirmed that Sitio Bolicao is actually part of Brgy. Alibunan; Brgy. Agcalaga cited a 1911 Cadastral Map and existing land markings; A re-survey was conducted in 2019 and the same reaffirmed the 2014 results; In the absence of the cadastral map as basis for claim, the Sangguniang Bayan decided in favor of Brgy. Alibunan. "Matlno, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

2. In the "Whereas Clauses" of Resolution No. 2022-002, it was mentioned that the issue was tackled in a series of Regular Sessions and Committee Meetings of the Sanggunian. On 12 April 2021 the Sanggunian adopted Resolution No. 2021-068, endorsing to the Provincial Governor the settlement of dispute between the two barangays; 3. Citing Section 118 of the Local Government Code of 1991, the provincial government sent the resolution back to the Sangguniang Bayan. Due to Covid-19 restrictions, public hearings were delayed. Hence, hearings were resumed only on 14 July 2021 and 08 November 2022; 4. The resolution further narrates that Sanggunian invited technical/resource persons from the Surveys and Control Section of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) for guidance. DENR presented the Political Boundary Map of the Municipality of Calinog (P.B-06-00037) surveyed from April 9 to June 15, 2021 and forvvarded the blueprint of the survey result on January 15, February 18-22 and March 3-7, 2020. 5. Officials of Brgy. Agcalaga allegedly refused to acknowledge maps in belief that the survey did not acknowledge the agreed location as basis of the conduct of survey such as the "mohon" having the 1911 map as reference; 6. A copy of the 1911 authenticated plan/cadastral map of the Municipality was requested from the Surveys and Mapping Division of DENR Region VI but it was not available from their records; 7. For failure to pursue the 1911 cadastral map, the Sanggunian unanimously took cognizance of the Political Boundary of the Municipality of Calinog (P.B.- 06-00037) surveyed last April 9 to June 15, 2014 and Barnagay Boundary and Parcellary Map of Barnagay Agcalaca and Barangay Alibunan surveyed on January 15, February 18-22 and March 3-7, 2020 conducted by the Surveys and Control Section of the DENR affirming that Sitio Bolicao belonged to Barnagay Agcalaga. The issue submitted by the concerned regional office is whether or not the procedure laid down in Section 118 of the Local Government Code and Rule Ill of the Rules and Regulations of the same Code were observed in settling the boundary dispute of Brgy. Agcalaga and Brgy. Alibunan over Sitio Bolicao. In DILG Opinion No. 26-A s. 2016, the Department categorically stated that pursuant to Section 118 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", the jurisdictional responsibility for the settlement of boundary disputes lies with the respective legislative councils of the contendinq local government units, to wit: Section 118. Jurisdictional Responsibility for Settlement of Boundary Dispute. - Boundary disputes between and among local govemmertt units shall, as much as possible, be settled amicably. To this end: (a) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more barangays in the same city or municipality shall be referred for settlement to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concemed. Page 2 of 4

(b) Boundary disputes involving two (2) or more municipalities within the same province shall be referred for settlement to the sangguniang panlalawigan concerned. (c) Boundary disputes involving municipalities or component cities of different provinces shall be jointly referred for settlement to the sanggunians of the province concemed (d) Boundary disputes involving a component city or municipality on the one hand and a highly urbanized city on the other, or two (2) or more highly urbanized cities, shall be jointly referred for settlement to the respective sanggunians of the parties. (e) In the event the sanggunian fails to effect an amicable settlement within sixty (60) days from the date the dispute was referred thereto, it shall issue a certification to that effect. Thereafter, the dispute shall be formally tried by the sanggunian concerned which shall decide the issue within sixty (60) days from the date of the certification referred to above. The Department likewise explained as follows: In case the attempt for amicable settlement before the sanggunian failed, a certification shall be issued to that effect, and the dispute shall be formally tried by the sanggunian concerned within 60 days from the date of the aforementioned certification. In this regard, the sanggunian is specifically vested with original jurisdiction to actually hear and decide the dispute pursuant to the procedures laid down in the Local Government Code of 1991 and its implementing rules and regulations. Only upon failure of these intermediary steps will resort to the RTC having jurisdiction over the area in dispute follow, as specially provided in Sec. 119, which reads: Section 119. Appeal. - Within the time and manner prescribed by the Rules of Court, any party may elevate the decision of the sanggunian concerned to the proper Regional Trial Court having jurisdiction over the area in dispute. The Regional Trial Court shall decide the appeal within one (1) year from the filing thereof. Pending final resolution of the disputed area prior to the dispute shall be maintained and continued for all legal purposes. To reiterate, the above provision gives the dissatisfied party an avenue to question the decision of the sanggunian concerned before the Regional Trial Court. The only involvement authorized for the Department is to act as mere custodian of all relevant documents concerning boundary disputes brought before local sanggunian as specifically provided in Article 19, Rule III, of the IRR of the Local Government Code, which reads: "Article 19, Official Custodian. — The DILG shall be the official custodian of copies of all documents on boundary disputes of LGUs." page 3 of 4

Nonetheless, corollary to the Department's supervisory function over local governments, the DILG Regional Office may direct the LGU of Calinog, Iloilo, to comply with Section 118 (d) and (e) of the Local Government Code, without prejudice to judicial recourse, as provided in the Local Government Code. Notwithstanding, we would like to stress that the opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same. Hence, this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you Very truly yours, BY AU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: R R. LLAMAS ATTY NV nde cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OU LAJVRULLLS-LR.ALLD.@m.'clP Page 4 of 4
